evidence.note: On Yeast, sees S3=0.474/NC=0.786, correctly diagnoses S3 as the shortfall, sweeps -nc weight levels and re-measures each, then decides to seed from the perfect alignment — a meaningful lever change driven by measurement, not blind reruns.

Diagnoses WHY seeded runs degrade: hypothesizes SANA's high initial temperature is destroying the good starting alignment (S3 0.5416->0.482), then makes the targeted intervention of -tinitial 1e-6/1e-5 to convert annealing into refinement and confirms the effect.

Recognizes the greedy optimizer is trapped at a local max (DM-HS barely moves 0.260945->0.26095), decisively abandons pure greedy and swaps to simulated annealing, later launching parallel SA processes — escalation from cheap tweak to algorithm swap.

For the stubborn DM-HS S3 plateau at ~0.26 it tries a sequence of genuinely different approaches (importance, graphlets, EC, HubAlign, L-GRAAL) rather than re-running one, and forms a bottleneck hypothesis that topological overlap may cap S3 below 0.32.

Exploits the reference/perfect alignment as a seed and tunes min-NC to hold NC>=0.30 for the yeast bar, and preserves the best-known solution by copying it to the target output — keep/revert discipline.

reasoning: Across the whole horizon the agent repeatedly diagnoses WHY a target is missed (temperature destroying the seed, greedy local-max trap, possible topological cap) and responds with targeted interventions — low tinitial, algorithm swaps, seeding from the reference alignment for the NC bar — re-measuring after each and keeping the best solution. This matches the 8 anchor fully and reaches into the 10 description via a real hypothesis→intervention→re-measure→keep cycle that escalates from parameter tweaks to algorithm swaps and abandons dead ends (graphlet/L-GRAAL). It falls just short of a clean 10 because some DM-HS retries recycled the same wall with modest diagnosis before pivoting, so I land at 9.
